When installing access points (APs) on high ceilings, what is the most common personal protective equipment (PPE) that should be used?
Hardhat, high visibility vest and body belt
Glasses, gloves and jacket
Clean suits, masks and glasses
Clean suits, gloves and jacket
A

High-ceiling work requires appropriate fall and impact protection. The listed hardhat, high-visibility vest, and body-belt combination addresses common site hazards; follow the site's actual fall-protection rules.
You are preparing to perform a site survey for a company that processes meat, but some areas are restricted due to high security. What should you do in order to proceed with the site survey?
Gain appropriate access and clearance to perform the site survey
Gain meat processing access certification from the FDA
Ensure that you and your team are using food industry approved USB adapters for the survey
Just begin the survey, they will understand
A
Obtain the required site access and security clearance before entering restricted areas. A survey must follow the customer's safety and access controls.
Which DHCP option, when required, must be configured to help access points (APs) locate their wireless LAN controller (WLC) during deployment?
C
DHCP Option 43 carries vendor-specific discovery information that compatible APs can use to learn the WLAN controller's IP address.

When deploying a new WLAN infrastructure using Power over Ethernet (PoE) to power the access points (APs), you find that a known good AP is not powering up. You connect your laptop using the same cable without any issues. What is the most likely reason the AP did not power up?
Missing AP licenses on the controller
Spanning-tree convergence
Layer 3 routing
Lack of PoE budget on the switch
D
PoE planning must use the maximum power the switch can supply per port and multiply it by the number of powered APs, while keeping the total within the switch's available budget.
During your first pre-deployment meeting with the deployment team, you hand out the full design documentation to everyone. What is your primary goal during this meeting?
To explain design decisions and ensure understanding of design documents
To discuss AP functionality
To explain how Wi-Fi works
To justify the budget
A
The kickoff meeting aligns installers with the design intent. Explaining the design decisions helps prevent field changes that undermine RF performance.
A controller-based WLAN infrastructure has its controller on a different subnet than its access points (APs). What device must be used to enable communication between the controller and the APs?
NTP server
Router
PoE Layer 2 switch
Wireless bridge
B
A router provides Layer 3 connectivity between different IP subnets so APs can reach a controller outside their local subnet.
What power management feature introduced in 802.11ax, but not available in 802.11ac or 802.11n, is designed to improve battery life for WLAN devices?
WMM-Power Save
Legacy Power Save
TWT
OFDMA
C
Target Wake Time schedules client wake periods, reducing unnecessary listening time and conserving battery power.
Aesthetics are critical in some environments. What common installation technique can best meet this requirement in a stadium while not voiding manufacturer warranties?
Painting to match team colors
Using enclosures under the seats
Mounting on a non-fixed pole
Mounting on the walls
B
Under-seat or handrail enclosures can conceal APs in a stadium while keeping them in a suitable location. Use manufacturer-approved enclosures to avoid compromising RF performance or warranty.
What type of site survey helps determine if roaming is functioning as intended?
Passive
Predictive
Active
Spectrum analysis walkthrough
C
An active survey associates to the WLAN and generates traffic while moving between APs, allowing roaming behavior and application continuity to be tested.

When performing a frame capture over the air during a voice call, you notice that frames in the downlink direction (from the AP to the client) are not being transmitted with the correct UP (User Priority) value for voice frames, but in the uplink direction (from the client to the AP), they are transmitted correctly. What is the likely cause of this issue?
Bad client driver
AP is not receiving enough PoE, thus not using QoS features
Somewhere on the wired network QoS markings aren't being trusted
Faulty antenna on the AP
C

The AP-to-client downlink priority is derived from the wired-side QoS markings. If the wired network does not trust or preserve DSCP markings, the AP can transmit frames with the wrong 802.11 User Priority.

You are validating client association capabilities to an 802.1X/EAP secure SSID. The RADIUS server's IP address is 10.100.50.25, and the default RADIUS authentication port is being used. None of the clients can associate with the SSID. After verifying that both the server and the RADIUS service are operational, you find that the authenticator (such as the AP or controller) is not communicating properly with the RADIUS server. What is your next troubleshooting step?
Verify that the shared secret between the authenticator and the RADIUS server is the correct
Reboot the clients to empty the shared secret cache
Reboot the server to empty the shared secret cache
Restart the RADIUS service to empty the shared secret cache
A
The RADIUS shared secret must match on the authenticator and server; a mismatch prevents valid RADIUS messages from being accepted.
During lunch time in the break room of a company, Wi-Fi connectivity on the 2.4 GHz band becomes intermittent. At other times of the day, it works fine. What is the most likely cause of this issue?
Employees are using their cell data instead of using the Wi-Fi
The AP in the cafeteria keeps rebooting due to lack of PoE budget on the switch
Toasters and ovens are heating up the air, raising the noise floor with the Wi-Fi on the 2.4 GHz band
Microwaves in the cafeteria are interfering with the Wi-Fi on the 2.4 GHz band
D
Microwave ovens operate in the 2.4 GHz range and can emit interference while heating. The lunch-time pattern points to microwave activity rather than a persistent WLAN configuration fault.

After deploying a 5 GHz-only WLAN infrastructure in the USA, using 20 MHz channel widths and all 25 available channels, a manager tests the Guest SSID on his 802.11n tablet. During testing, he experiences several areas with poor RSSI (below -80 dBm) or no signal at all. Upon checking, all APs are operational, and coverage was validated post-deployment. What is the likely cause of this issue?
His tablet doesn't support the 5 GHz band
His tablet only supports a 40 MHz channel-width
His tablet does not support one or more of the 5 GHz channels
His tablet doesn't support MU-MIMO
C
Not all client radios support every 5 GHz channel. A channel unsupported by the client will not appear during scanning, even if other clients can connect.

After designing and deploying a WLAN infrastructure, you notice that co-channel interference (CCI) is causing poor performance in the 2.4 GHz band. Although the WLAN was primarily designed for 5 GHz, 2.4 GHz was included as a best-effort solution. You discover that the implementers did not follow your configuration guidelines. What can you do to minimize the impact of CCI in the 2.4 GHz band without adding adjacent-channel interference (ACI)?
Add more APs to the infrastructure
Increase the transmit power on all APs
Turn off 2.4 GHz radios on some APs
Use all channels available in the 2.4 GHz band
C
Disabling selected 2.4 GHz radios reduces the number of co-channel contenders. This is preferable to adding more APs or raising power, which can worsen CCI.

You have performed a validation site survey after deploying a WLAN infrastructure in an All-Wireless- Office. One specific application is experiencing delays after transitioning from wired to wireless connectivity. During validation, you discover that all APs are using 80 MHz channel widths instead of the designed 20 MHz on the 5 GHz band. What can be done to resolve the delay for this application?
APs should be using 160 MHz channel-widths to get more throughput
Reconfigure to use 20 MHz channel-widths, so reuse of the frequency is more effective
Power-off half of the APs to reduce CCI and keep 80 MHz channel-widths
Add more APs using 80 MHz channel-widths
B
Narrower channels provide more opportunities for channel reuse and reduce the number of APs competing on the same spectrum, often improving capacity in dense WLANs.
What deliverables should be provided to the customer after successfully implementing a WLAN infrastructure?
Digital or physical assets, guides, floorplans with design information, and configuration documents
Project Charter, requirements specification, and software licenses
Facility blueprints, NDAs, and hold harmless documents
Nothing is required. The implemented WLAN was the deliverable.
A
Closeout should include the physical or digital assets, configuration records, guides, and annotated floor plans needed to operate and maintain the WLAN.
Who should be present from the customer side during the final meeting after successfully implementing a WLAN infrastructure?
Acquirer and stakeholders
End-users
The customer's customers
Remote workers
A
Project closeout should transfer the agreed documentation, configurations, assets, and operational knowledge to the customer stakeholders.

During a validation site survey, you discover that some access points (APs) have been mounted above the ceiling due to an aesthetic request from the building architect. However, no aesthetics constraints were communicated during the requirements gathering from the main stakeholder of the project. What is the appropriate course of action?
Advise the stakeholder that WLAN performance requirements will not be met and a new design process will be needed to meet the requirements
Leave it as it is and allow automatic channel management to correct any issues
Increase the output power on all APs by 6 dB immediately to accommodate for the additional attenuation
Remove all external antennas and use only the internal antennas to reduce multipath and increase acquirer satisfaction
A

Mounting APs above the ceiling adds unplanned attenuation and changes the designed antenna environment. The stakeholder must be told that the original performance requirements may not be met and the design must be revisited.
According to IEEE 29148-2018, which of the following is a characteristic of a requirements set that is not a characteristic of an individual requirement statement?
Comprehensible
Feasible
Necessary
Verifiable
A
A requirements set must be understandable as a coherent collection. Individual requirements are also evaluated for qualities such as necessity, feasibility, and verifiability.

In a convention center auditorium, you've received complaints about the WLAN performance. Currently, only two APs are installed, but they are supporting over 300 client devices simultaneously, which exceeds the original design. What action should you take to ensure the Wi-Fi works as expected?
Redesign the WLAN for the auditorium requirement area
Quickly add more APs to the auditorium requirement area
Upgrade the Ethernet connections to MultiGig
Turn up the output power on the APs so that they can handle more clients
A
When user density exceeds the original design assumptions, redesign capacity for the actual client count and application demand rather than simply turning up AP power.
In 802.11, clients are required to be calibrated for RSSI and SNR reporting to:
Within +/−5 dB
Within +/−3 dB
Within +/−1 dB
Within +/−0.5 dB
Within +/−0.25 dB
No specific value
F
The 802.11 specifications do not require client RSSI/SNR reports to meet one universal calibration tolerance. Reported values can vary by client implementation.

You have determined the best mounting locations for APs in a given installation. The facilities manager has asked you to change the locations for several APs due to aesthetic concerns. You suggest mounting the APs in the ideal locations and painting them so they go unnoticed in the environment. What is a valid recommendation or consideration when painting APs?
Always use paints with metallic dye in them to prevent potential RF propagation impact.
Painting APs will significantly reduce the output power.
Painting APs may void the product manufacturer's warranty.
Most AP models for indoor environments come in a variety of form factors and colors. Painting is never recommended.
C
Painting an AP can alter its materials or ventilation and may violate the manufacturer's installation instructions, potentially voiding the product warranty.
When deploying long-distance 802.11 bridge links (10 miles / 16 km), what parameter may be critical for improving data flow by reducing retries caused by the long distances?
The sequence control field value
The acknowledgement timeout threshold
The minimum transmit data rate value
The CTS-to-self threshold
B
Long-distance propagation delay can exceed default ACK timers. The acknowledgement timeout must account for the round-trip delay so valid frames are not treated as lost.

One of your customers plans on providing wireless coverage to a warehouse facility. After performing an initial walkthrough, you collect the following information: The central part of the warehouse is between 400 and 600 feet (122 to 183 meters) from the warehouse switches mounted on the walls. The warehouse storage is composed of metallic racks with varying inventory levels and contents, from electronics and plastic toys to food pallets and juice bottles. Workers need basic data coverage from their working location, and are not highly mobile. They usually work from one single aisle, and their laptop is on a cart with wheels. What would be your one recommendation to provide coverage to the central area of the warehouse?
Equip workers laptops with a directional antenna and install APs less than 328 feet (100m) away from the switch.
In this case, extend the cable length just beyond 328 feet (100 m) and position APs as close as possible to the central area of the warehouse.
Position APs along the walls, and equip the APs with Yagi antennas to cover the central area.
Install APs for client access in the central area and use a mesh backhaul link to connect to the DS.
B

The supplied answer key selects extending the cable run beyond 100 m, but standard copper Ethernet channel limits are generally 100 m. This answer appears technically questionable; use a fiber uplink, intermediate switch, or other compliant design rather than exceeding the limit.
Which definition correctly describes the "local MAC" variation of the centralized WLAN architecture?
All MAC functions are performed by the AP. A minimal subset of network control is offloaded to the WLAN controller along with management and monitoring functions.
PHY functions are performed directly by the AP. MAC functions are divided almost equally between the WLAN controller and the AP, according to the time sensitivity of the feature or service.

The AP provides the RF termination point for the WLAN, but performs very few of the WLAN functions or services. The WLAN controller performs all MAC functions and the AP is very simple and lightweight.
All RF-, data-, and control-related WLAN functions are performed by the AP. APs coordinate network services with one another and are managed by a WNMS,
A
In a local-MAC design, the AP performs the MAC functions locally. The controller retains selected network-control, management, and monitoring responsibilities.
When a WLAN controller sends an 802.11 frame to a lightweight AP for transmission on the wireless medium, how does it mark the frame for 802.11 QoS priority?
The WLAN controller will place the user priority (UP) value in the QoS Control field of the 802.11 frame header before passing it to the lightweight AP.
The WLAN controller does not mark 802.11 frames with priority values only the APs can do this.
The WLAN controller does not mark the 802.11 frames with priority values only the Layer 3 switches can do this.
The WLAN controller does not mark the 802.11 frames with priority values only the Layer 3 routers can do this.
A
The 802.11 QoS Control field carries the User Priority value used to classify and prioritize wireless frames.
When selecting a centralized WLAN architecture, what new problem may arise when you change the data forwarding model from centralized to distributed?
APs that were designed for a centralized forwarding model may not support all features in distributed forwarding mode.
The router between the APs and the controller must be made aware of the APs as forwarding client STAs.
All RRM controls will also need to be distributed to a master AP that acts as a channel and transmit power arbiter for other APs in the ESS.
Centralized control functions, such as key management and distribution, RRM, and load balancing will no longer be supported.
A
Distributed forwarding can expose capability gaps: an AP designed primarily for centralized forwarding may not implement every feature required when client traffic is switched locally.
Which one of the following is an essential metric to measure when performing a survey and design for VoIP across WLANs?
Throughput rates above 50 Mbps
Data rates above 100 Mbps
Latency
PoE provided to wireless handsets
C
Latency directly affects conversational quality. Excessive delay makes voice conversations feel sluggish even when throughput is adequate.

In a manufacturing facility with highly reflective materials, you are planning an upgrade to your existing 802.11b WLAN implementation. You have chosen a dual-band 802.11n infrastructure product for this purpose. Your client applications include: Handheld scanners for inventory management; Toughbooks (laptops) mounted on forklifts for inventory and workflow management; VoWiFi phones used by select employees throughout the facility. You are evaluating all of the 802.11n enhancements and determining which features to enable for your environment and applications. In this scenario, what 802.11n enhancement typically should NOT be enabled on the 2.4 GHz radio of the new APs?
Multiple streams
Short guard intervals
Block Acknowledgments
Frame aggregation
B

Short guard intervals reduce symbol spacing and can increase throughput, but reflective environments create multipath delay spread; the longer guard interval is generally safer in such conditions. The supplied answer key selects short guard intervals, so verify this item against your reference before relying on it.
When implementing WLAN security according to common best practices, what feature should be enabled when configuring an EAP type?
The "Use WEP if RADIUS server unavailable" option
The "Validate server certificate" option
The "Trusted Root Certification Authorities" list
The "Do not prompt user to authorize new servers or trusted certification authorities" option
B
Validating the RADIUS server certificate helps ensure the client is connecting to the legitimate authentication server and prevents credential theft through a rogue server.
You are selecting external antennas for use in a bridge link deployment. What chart should you request from the antenna vendors to make an accurate selection?
mW to dBm conversion chart
dBm to dB conversion chart
Elevation chart
Antenna coating chart
C
An antenna elevation chart shows the vertical radiation pattern and beamwidth, which is essential for selecting an antenna for a bridge link and aligning it in elevation.
When live video streaming solutions that transmit simultaneously to more than one recipient are used, what special capability should be considered and configured in all affected WLAN implementations?
IPSec
IPv6
Multicasting
Secure TCP
C
Multicast lets one sender distribute the same stream to multiple receivers without creating a separate full-rate stream for each client.
What VoWiFi implementations frequently require multicast packet delivery support by the WLAN infrastructure?
All VoWiFi implementations
Push-to-Talk VoWiFi phones
All VoWiFi soft phones
All VoWiFi hard phones
B
Multicast lets one sender distribute the same stream to multiple receivers without creating a separate full-rate stream for each client.

As you plan a WLAN upgrade, you have assessed the network requirements and data signatures of your applications. One of the popular applications used on your network requires high bandwidth and low to medium Wi-Fi loss, but can tolerate moderate latency and jitter. What application matches this description?
Voice
Email
Skype chat
Video-on-demand
B

The supplied key selects Email, but the described profile (high bandwidth with tolerance for moderate latency and jitter) is more characteristic of buffered video delivery. Verify this item against the intended source answer before using it for scoring.

Given: The 802.11ac APs you have selected for your public access deployment support many of the PHY and MAC enhancements offered by the 802.11n and 802.11ac amendments. The AP is configured for a single-band (2.4 GHz) and only allows 20 MHz channels. The WLAN radio in the AP is a 3x3 802.11n chip that supports two spatial streams. What is the maximum MCS rate that could be supported by this AP?
54 Mbps
65 Mbps
108 Mbps
144 Mbps
D
A 20 MHz 802.11n channel with two spatial streams and a short guard interval supports a maximum PHY rate of approximately 144.4 Mbps.

As an implementation engineer, you have just received initial design specs from a network designer for your dual-band 802.11n deployment. The network design documents prescribe the following data rate configuration for the 2.4 GHz radio: Basic Rates 5.5, 6, 11, 12 Mbps Supported Rates 9, 18, 24, 36, 48, and 54 Mbps as well as MCS 0-15 What will result from this design strategy?
By disabling support for 1 and 2 Mbps while allowing 5.5 and 11 Mbps, the network will force 802.11b clients to use these higher data rates.
Protection mechanisms will always be in use on this network to support 5.5 and 11 Mbps as basic rates.
HR/DSSS (802.11b) stations will not be able to associate to the service set.
This configuration violates the IEEE specification that defines 6, 12, and 24 Mbps as mandatory data rates for 802.11g/n.
A
Disabling the 1 and 2 Mbps rates removes the slowest legacy rates, encouraging supported clients to use faster rates and reducing airtime consumed by very slow transmissions.

Given: As the wireless network administrator for XYZ Company, you are planning to upgrade your aging wireless network infrastructure, as well as some clients, to support 802.11ac. In your research, you have discovered that your new wireless client devices and infrastructure are 802.11ac, WMM, and WMM-PS certified by the Wi-Fi Alliance. Some of your existing client devices are 802.11a/b/g devices that do not support WMM. Given this information, what scenario is possible when your company's employees begin using both types of client devices on the new WLAN?
All WMM-PS certified client devices will be prevented from utilizing WMM-PS features until all stations in use on the wireless medium are WMM-PS certified.
The WLAN infrastructure will set the dozing times of the WMM-PS certified client devices based upon their WMM access category, while the non-WMM-PS client devices will continue to use PS-Poll frames.
Performance and battery life will be inconsistent between WMM-PS and non-WMM-PS client devices when used with applications that support WMM-PS.
WMM-PS enabled APs will allow both WMM-PS and non-WMM-PS stations to use the trigger-and-delivery mechanism, but WMM-PS stations will
C

WMM-PS clients use trigger-based power-save delivery, while older non-WMM clients use legacy power-save behavior. Mixed client capabilities can therefore produce different performance and battery-life outcomes.

You desire to achieve a 450 Mbps MCS. What 802.11n features (from the numbered list below) are required? 1. Frame aggregation 2. Short GI 3. 40 MHz channels 4. 2 spatial streams 5. 3 spatial streams 6. Transmit beamforming (TxBF)
D
A 450 Mbps 802.11n PHY rate requires 40 MHz channel width, short guard interval, and three spatial streams.

You are tasked with designing the WLAN to accommodate certain high density areas on your university campus where users frequently come and go. With a limited DHCP pool size (subnet mask = 255.255.252.0) for this WLAN subnet, you want to ensure that your DHCP addresses are used efficiently and are not exhausted, which would prevent new client Layer 3 connections. The DHCP server is a Windows Server 2012 R2 machine. Your design task is to determine the best configuration to allow as many users as possible while avoiding WLAN service interruptions and also to use the available addresses as efficiently as possible. What setting would be most effective at achieving this design task?
Set the RTS threshold to 2346 bytes
Set the inactive wireless client timeout (client age-out) to 5 minutes
Set the maximum client limit per radio to 64
Set the DHCP lease for this pool to 20 minutes
D
A WLAN with many clients needs enough DHCP addresses and appropriate lease management so address exhaustion does not prevent new associations from obtaining IP connectivity.
What is the DSCP Per Hop Behavior equivalent classification of the 802.11 AC_VO priority level?
AF31
CS3
VO
EF
D
The 802.11 AC_VO voice access category maps to the EF (Expedited Forwarding) DiffServ per-hop behavior, which is commonly used for low-latency voice traffic.
